$comment: HZ-135. Input/expected pairs for the work-item priority bindings, asserted by BOTH server/test/domain-priorities-cases.test.mjs and farm/tests/test_priorities_fixtures.py. The `shared` section is the point of the file: domain/js/priorities.js and domain/py/priorities.py are two independent hand-written implementations, and without this nothing would prove a validation rule or a membership check meant the same thing in both languages — the same gap domain/fixtures/lifecycle-cases.json and fields-cases.json were added to close. Every case in `shared` runs in both suites, and each suite asserts it executed the exact ids listed in shared.manifest, so a suite cannot quietly skip a section and still pass. The `js` and `py` sections cover the exports that exist in only one binding; a coverage guard in each suite asserts SET EQUALITY between that section's keys and the binding's real exports, so a new export with no case fails, and a stale case naming a removed export fails too. Every priority value in this file is FABRICATED on purpose — not one real value appears, so the fixture is not a second declaration of the vocabulary and does not have to be allowlisted by domain-priority-literals.test.mjs.
